description: We are six software developers from Zone01 Kisumu, a project-based coding school in Kenya. We build with Go, JavaScript and cloud tools, and our members are specializing in cloud and DevOps, AI, blockchain and full-stack web development. We want to turn NASA's open data into a working, deployed application that people can actually use, and to represent Kisumu and East Africa at Space Apps.
summary: We developed a mobile and backend system pairing a Go microservice API with a Flutter mobile app utilizing the Carbon Design System. It integrates NASA Earth Observations (POWER, SMAP, GPM, and SRTM) with regional soil physics, a Gorgonia neural network machine learning engine, and a specialized agronomic crop catalog.
details:
• Geospatial Onboarding: A user selects their farm location on an interactive OpenStreetMap interface within the mobile app.
  • Live Telemetry Aggregation: The Go backend immediately queries NASA Earth Observation APIs using those exact coordinates. It aggregates 14-day precision telemetry, 12-month timelines, and multi-year climate baselines.
  • Environmental Synthesizing: The platform evaluates subterranean Drought Stress Index using NASA SMAP, historical precipitation patterns using NASA GPM, and terrain characteristics using NASA SRTM.
  • Intelligent Optimization: A native Go neural network processes these data vectors alongside regional soil profiles and an agronomic database to score crop suitability, highlight bare soil vulnerabilities, and map out optimal, climate-resilient crop rotation sequences.
projectRefs: Gorgonia Graph Computation Engine for Go
